pr.title: fix data race in GetWebAssets

raw_findings.body: Every queued goroutine re-runs `readWebAssetsFromFile` (disk open + JSON decode of assets-manifest.json) and overwrites `entryPointAssetsCache`, serialized behind the exclusive lock, so N concurrent first requests pay N sequential manifest parses instead of one; the cache provides no protection against the initial stampede.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Redundant, serialized filesystem/JSON work on every concurrent cache miss; latency spike proportional to concurrency at startup.
raw_findings.impact: Every queued goroutine re-runs `readWebAssetsFromFile` (disk open + JSON decode of assets-manifest.json) and overwrites `entryPointAssetsCache`, serialized behind the exclusive lock, so N concurrent first requests pay N sequential manifest parses instead of one; the cache provides no protection against the initial stampede.
raw_findings.root_cause: The added lock upgrade from RLock to Lock does not re-validate the cache state that may have been filled by another goroutine while this goroutine was not holding any lock.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: After acquiring the write lock, re-check `if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil { return entryPointAssetsCache, nil }` before doing any CDN/file read, completing the double-checked locking pattern.
raw_findings.title: Write-locked path lacks a re-check of the cache (broken double-checked locking)
raw_findings.trigger: Cold start in a non-dev environment: several concurrent HTTP requests (e.g. `/api/frontend/assets` and index page loads) call `GetWebAssets` before the cache is populated. All of them observe `ret == nil` under the read lock and then queue on `entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()`.

raw_findings.body: The regression this patch fixes is untested: `go test -race` will not detect reintroduction of the unsynchronized read/write of `entryPointAssetsCache`.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Review/CI cannot verify the race fix or prevent its regression.
raw_findings.impact: The regression this patch fixes is untested: `go test -race` will not detect reintroduction of the unsynchronized read/write of `entryPointAssetsCache`.
raw_findings.root_cause: Synchronization was added without accompanying test coverage for the concurrent access path it guards.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add a test in `pkg/api/webassets/webassets_test.go` that launches multiple goroutines calling `GetWebAssets` with a non-dev `setting.Cfg` pointing at `testdata/` and a fake licensing service, so `-race` covers the new locking.
raw_findings.title: No concurrency/race test added for the newly synchronized global asset cache
raw_findings.trigger: The patch's stated purpose is fixing a data race on `entryPointAssetsCache`, but `pkg/api/webassets/webassets_test.go` only exercises `readWebAssetsFromFile`/`readWebAssetsFromCDN`; no test calls `GetWebAssets` concurrently, so a future change that drops or narrows the lock passes CI.

Multiple goroutines observing ret==nil under RLock will all queue on Lock and each will execute readWebAssetsFromFile sequentially. The cited lines exist verbatim, the cause is introduced by this patch, the trigger (concurrent cold-start requests) is realistic, and the impact (N sequential manifest parses instead of 1) follows directly from the code.
